r-0001.title: Prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
r-0001.notes: The rule covers residential dwelling units in Berkeley with no building-level limits. The exemptions are product-based (aggregated anonymous data publishers, affordable housing limit-setting tools, market research or software testing tools). They do not turn on building characteristics, so no tests are written for them. Rent Ordinance coverage and exemption criteria from related records are not incorporated here because ch. 13.63 does not reference them.

r-0002.title: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees (BMC 13.78.010)
r-0002.notes: Coverage applies to any owner or agent who charges a screening fee for residential property in Berkeley. No building-level limits or exemptions are stated, so no tests are needed. The condition that a fee is charged is a behavioral trigger, not a building attribute.

r-0003.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees for existing tenancies (BMC 13.78.016)
r-0003.notes: Coverage is all residential rental agreements in Berkeley (BMC 13.78.018) with no stated exemptions, so there are no building-level limits. Rent Ordinance coverage and exemptions in related records concern other rules and were not applied.

r-0004.title: Berkeley just cause eviction rules as amended by Measure BB

tests.source_text: university rental units such as dormitories
tests.note: Dormitories and university rental units are exempt; apartments pass.

tests.source_text: owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property when the tenancy started
tests.note: Shared-kitchen/bath exemption depends on the landlord's residence at the start of the tenancy, which the data cannot see. Engine should answer unknown.

tests.source_text: Exempt: 'Golden Duplex'
tests.note: Golden Duplex is a duplex owner-occupied on Dec 31, 1979 and currently; the data cannot see owner occupancy. A duplex is needed for it to be possible.

tests.source_text: tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied
tests.note: Depends on ADU presence, owner occupancy and tenancy start date, which the data cannot see. Engine should answer unknown.

tests.source_text: nonprofit cooperatives
tests.note: Ownership structure is not visible in the data.

r-0004.notes: Both fully and partially covered units are subject to just cause, so there is no year_built or certificate-of-occupancy limit; the build-date and tenancy-date distinctions only change the coverage category. Only the listed exemptions limit coverage. Owner-move-in and Ellis Act text describes eviction grounds, not coverage, so it is not turned into a test.

r-0005.title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA), Rent Board Regulation 1148

tests.source_text: Not rent controlled: new construction built and issued a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980
tests.note: Berkeley rent control excludes new construction with a certificate of occupancy after June 1980. The text gives only month and year, so June 1, 1980 is used as the cutoff. The engine treats the certificate-of-occupancy date as unknown and uses year_built as a proxy.

tests.source_text: single-family home tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 1996; most condominiums
tests.note: Single-family homes are fully covered only if the tenancy began before 1996, and most condominiums are not rent controlled. Single-family and condo types are treated as not applicable, which is a conservative simplification. Tenancy start cannot be seen from the data.

tests.source_text: university rental units such as dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives
tests.note: Exempt from the ordinance.

tests.source_text: 'Golden Duplex' (owner-occupied on December 31, 1979 and currently has an owner in one unit); owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property when the tenancy started; tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied
tests.note: Owner-occupancy exemptions that the data cannot see.

r-0005.notes: The criteria come from the related D006 and D009 statements on fully covered units: most multifamily built before 1980, and single-family homes whose tenancies began before 1996. Partially covered and exempt units are not subject to the AGA ceiling.
r-0005.review_ruling: instructions/rulings_05.md #2: tenancy length is a tenant-level fact that decides when an increase may be taken, not whether the building is covered. Drop the tenancy_months test; keep COO 1980 cutoff, condo/single-family, dormitory/co-op and golden-duplex tests.

r-0006.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance

tests.source_text: owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence
tests.note: Owner occupancy cannot be seen in the data, so the engine cannot confirm it. The exemption only applies to 1-3 unit properties.

tests.source_text: limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties
tests.note: Subsidy status is not visible in the data. The exemption is described as limited and its scope is not detailed.

tests.source_text: units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
tests.note: Tenancy circumstances are not visible in the data.

tests.source_text: units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9
tests.note: Lease terms are not visible in the data.

r-0006.notes: Coverage is all rental housing providers in Berkeley, with no building-level limits. Every test is an exemption the data cannot see. The lifetime sex offender exemption concerns the applicant, not the building, so it has no test.

r-0007.title: Berkeley security deposit interest coverage

tests.source_text: university rental units such as dormitories
tests.note: Dormitory/university units are exempt; an apartment building passes.

tests.source_text: Exempt: 'Golden Duplex'
tests.note: Golden Duplex exemption depends on owner occupancy on Dec 31, 1979 and currently; the data cannot see this. A duplex is the only possible case.

tests.source_text: nonprofit cooperatives
tests.note: Nonprofit cooperative status is not visible in the data.

tests.source_text: owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property when the tenancy started
tests.note: Owner-occupancy and shared facilities are not visible in the data.

tests.source_text: tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied
tests.note: ADU and owner-occupancy status are not visible in the data.

r-0007.notes: Coverage is stated as fully or partially covered units (multifamily pre-1980, post-1980 new construction, single-family, most condos, certain subsidized units), which together span nearly all residential types. This gives no building-level limit, and the 'covered by the Rent Ordinance' wording is circular, so no coverage test is written. Only the exemptions become tests.

r-0008.title: [notice-only] Boston Housing Stability Notification Act

tests.source_text: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
tests.note: Institutional/care-facility exclusion; an ordinary apartment or house passes.

r-0008.notes: Coverage is all landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy in Boston, with no unit-count, age, or owner-type limits. The only exemption is for health-care and substance-abuse treatment facility residences. Notice-only ordinance.

r-0011.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy - criminal history

tests.value: DND funding/land or BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted unit
tests.source_text: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy
tests.note: Subsidy/funding status is not visible in address data; applies only to providers with DND funding/land or BPDA IDP income-restricted units, not all Boston landlords.

r-0011.notes: Coverage depends on funding/agreement status, which the engine cannot see. Exemptions (direct relationship between conviction and housing, unreasonable risk to safety, current criminal behavior, conflicting federal/state requirements) are tenant/applicant-specific and not building-level, so no tests are produced for them.

r-0012.title: Boston fair housing protection for renters using rental assistance
r-0012.notes: Coverage is housing in the City of Boston with no stated exemptions and no building-level limits. The 'renters and applicants using rental assistance' condition describes the protected class, not a building characteristic, so no test is written for it. The related records' exemptions belong to other rules (just-cause notice and the DND-funded Fair Chance policy) and do not describe who is covered by or exempt from this rule.

r-0013.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
r-0013.notes: General antitrust law that applies to any industry, not only rental housing, so there are no building-level limits. The exclusions for end consumers and for single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data concern the actor and the algorithm, not the address. They cannot be tested with address facts and are not building-level limits.

r-0014.title: California application screening fee cap and conditions (Civ. Code § 1950.6)
r-0014.notes: The rule covers any landlord or agent charging a screening fee to an applicant for residential rental housing. No building-level limits are stated. The only exemption is non-preemption of federal or state housing assistance program rules on deposits and fees. That is not a building-level test and is not tied to anything the data can see, so no test is written for it.

r-0015.title: California Tenant Protection Act - just cause for termination

tests.source_text: Transient/tourist hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended-care and licensed care facilities; school dormitories
tests.note: Excluded institutional and transient categories.

tests.source_text: housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years
tests.note: New construction exempt for 15 years; year_built used as proxy with cutoff year treated as unknown.

tests.source_text: Tenant has occupied for 12 months (or 24 months if an additional adult tenant was added before an existing tenant reached 24 months)
tests.note: Tenancy length is not visible in the data; protection attaches only after 12 months (24 in the added-tenant case).

tests.source_text: owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex; shared bathroom/kitchen with owner-occupant; separately alienable property not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, with written exemption notice
tests.note: Owner identity and occupancy are not visible. The separately alienable property exemption also requires written notice to the tenant. Multi-unit apartment buildings are not exempt on this basis.

tests.source_text: deed-restricted affordable housing
tests.note: Deed restriction or subsidy status is not visible in the data.

r-0015.notes: Mobilehome owners are also exempt. Not applicable where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before 2019-09-01, or a later more protective one, covers the property. The section is repealed 2030-01-01. Query date 2026-10-01.

r-0016.title: Statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act), Civ. Code § 1947.12

tests.source_text: The cap does not apply to housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome).
tests.note: Rolling 15-year new-construction exemption; the engine uses year_built as a proxy for the certificate-of-occupancy date.

tests.source_text: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing
tests.note: Deed-restricted or subsidized housing is exempt. The engine cannot see subsidy status, so this is unknown.

tests.source_text: dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school
tests.note: Only dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school are exempt.

tests.source_text: separately alienable property (e.g. single-family homes, condos) whose owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, and where the required written exemption notice was given
tests.note: The single-family or condo exemption depends on the owner type and on the written notice. The engine cannot see either, so this is unknown. Multi-unit apartment buildings are not separately alienable, so the exception cannot apply to them.

tests.source_text: a duplex in which the owner occupies one unit as a principal residence
tests.note: The duplex owner-occupancy exemption cannot be seen by the engine. It is impossible for buildings that are not duplexes.

r-0016.notes: The statewide cap applies to residential property older than 15 years, using year_built as a proxy for the certificate-of-occupancy date. Exemptions for local rent control stricter than the state cap, mobilehome homeowners, and the two-unit owner-occupied case are not visible in the address data. Date limits (March 15, 2019 and February 18, 2021 for mobilehomes) are look-back application dates, not building-level tests. The statute is repealed as of 2030-01-01, after the query date.

r-0017.title: Criminal history screening limits (Civil Rights Council regulations)
r-0017.notes: Coverage is housing decisions by landlords in California using criminal history information, with no building-level limits and no exemptions stated. Related records describe other rules' exemptions (e.g. owner-occupied or small-landlord carve-outs for other rules), which do not state exemptions for this rule's category, so none are applied.

r-0018.title: Source-of-income discrimination ban and subsidy-tenant credit/income screening limits (FEHA)
r-0018.notes: The ban covers owners of any housing accommodation, so there are no building-level limits. The subd. (o) credit-history and income-standard rules apply only where a government rent subsidy exists, but subsidy status is not visible at the address level, so no test is written for it. The owner-occupied one-additional-person exclusion mentioned in the FAQ is not stated to apply to source of income, so it is not turned into a test. The exemption for inquiring about the level or source of income is a conduct carve-out, not a building-level exemption.

r-0019.title: California residential security deposit cap and return rules (Civ. Code § 1950.5)

tests.source_text: The two-month cap applies if the landlord is a natural person or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
tests.note: This only governs whether the 2-month small-landlord cap applies instead of the 1-month cap. The base 1-month cap covers all residential rentals. The engine cannot see owner identity, so this is unknown for the small-landlord tier.

r-0019.notes: The base rule (one-month cap, 21-day return, no 'nonrefundable' label) covers all residential dwelling rentals. The only building-level fact tied to the small-landlord tier is the four-unit ceiling, so a building with more than 4 units cannot qualify for the 2-month tier. The service-member, six-month-advance-payment and pre-July-1-2024 exemptions are tenancy- or transaction-specific and are not visible to the engine.

r-0020.title: Cambridge policy order initiating ban on algorithmic rent-setting services
r-0020.notes: The policy order covers residential property managers in general. The 'large or corporate' wording is descriptive and gives no numeric or building-level limit. No exemptions are stated. The exemptions in the related records belong to other rules (tenant rights notification, fair housing) and do not describe this rule's category, so they are not applied. The measure is only a proposal and not enacted law.

r-0021.title: [notice-only] Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance (Cambridge M.C. ch. 8.71)

tests.source_text: Rental units in a hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, or in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term assistance, treatment or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse; Short Term Rental Units under Cambridge Zoning Ordinance Art. 4, Sec. 4.60.
tests.note: Excludes institutional/care facilities and short-term rental units; an ordinary apartment building passes.

r-0021.notes: Notice-only ordinance applying to residential rental agreements generally (including a single dwelling unit and tenants at will). The only limits are the facility and short-term-rental exemptions. No unit-count, age, or owner-type limits are stated.

r-0022.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance: source-of-income protection (incl. Section 8)

tests.source_text: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
tests.note: Exemption applies only to owner-occupied 2-family dwellings; the engine cannot see owner occupancy, so owner_type is checked and is unknown at address level. Duplexes may be exempt if the owner lives there.

r-0022.notes: Rule covers all rental housing transactions in Cambridge except owner-occupied 2-family dwellings. Owner occupancy is not visible to the engine. Buildings that are not 2-family (units != 2, or building_type not duplex) cannot qualify for the exemption. Ordinance text itself is not in the corpus; only a secondary summary.

r-0023.title: Algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing market prohibited

tests.source_text: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from 'residential dwelling unit'.
tests.note: Excludes medical, long-term care and detention facilities; apartments and other residences pass.

r-0023.notes: Covers any residential dwelling unit (primary residence) in Hoboken; the only building-level limit is the exclusion of medical/long-term care and detention facilities. Possible preemption by NJ FAIR Act is not a building-level test. Rent control applicability in related records is a separate rule and not used.

r-0024.title: Mandatory disclosures for rental increases over 10%
r-0024.notes: Coverage is all residential landlords raising rent by more than 10% on renewal for a current tenant, and no exemptions are stated. The 10% increase is the trigger for the disclosure duty, not a building-level limit, so no test is written for it. The related rent control record (Chapter 155) concerns a different rule, so its incomplete applicability does not carry over.

r-0025.title: Hoboken Rent Control: annual rent increase cap (§ 155-5)

tests.source_text: Motels and hotels
tests.note: Hotels and motels are exempt from rent control.

tests.source_text: multiple dwellings built after June 25, 1987 for the lesser of mortgage amortization or 30 years (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1)
tests.note: Exemption depends on mortgage term and filings the data cannot show. A newer building is unknown, not excluded.

r-0025.notes: Other exemptions (newly constructed dwellings on first rental, industrial/commercial property, school-owned, government-owned, vacant since 1984, condo/co-op owner-occupant decontrol) depend on facts not in the data and are not tested. Coverage is stated as all dwelling units except those exempt under § 155-2, so coverage is not marked incomplete.

r-0026.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
r-0026.notes: This rule lists no coverage conditions or exemptions, so no building-level tests are written. A related record describes the ban as covering landlords/owners of multifamily rental housing, but it is a secondary-source article that does not reproduce the ordinance text and gives no unit threshold, so it is not turned into a test. The 1-4 unit exemption belongs to the rent control ordinance, not this rule. The reported exclusions (real estate agents, owners not colluding, MLS) concern the kind of actor or conduct, not the building. Possible preemption by the NJ FAIR Act is not addressed.

r-0027.title: Jersey City ban on rent-setting algorithms (RealPage-type software)

tests.source_text: Landlords/owners of multifamily rental housing in Jersey City
tests.note: Article describes coverage as multifamily rental housing but gives no unit threshold. Multifamily is read as 5 or more units, consistent with the 1-4 unit exemption in the rent control chapter, but that exemption belongs to a different rule and is only a proxy. The ordinance text is not reproduced.

r-0027.notes: Coverage comes only from a secondary news article and the ordinance text is not captured. The article's exemptions (real estate agents; owners using algorithms without colluding; an unclear Multiple Listing Service outcome) turn on the user's conduct and cannot be read from address facts, so no tests were written for them. Possible NJ FAIR Act preemption is not modeled.

r-0028.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance (Municipal Code Chapter 260)

tests.source_text: all 1-4 unit properties are exempt
tests.note: 1-4 unit properties are exempt, so the rule applies only to properties with 5 or more units. The page also mentions other permitted exemptions (via a 'Rent Control Exemption Request') but does not list their criteria.

r-0028.notes: The page only states the 1-4 unit exemption. The other permitted exemptions under Ch. 260 are not described, so they cannot be tested. The rent increase cap formula is not stated.

r-0029.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)

tests.source_text: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, ... some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance-abuse treatment centers
tests.note: Excludes the exempt facility types; apartment buildings pass.

tests.source_text: Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
tests.note: Tenancy length is not visible to the engine, so this condition cannot be checked from address data.

tests.source_text: owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless facilities ... and some HACLA or government-owned properties
tests.note: Owner identity and occupancy are not visible to the engine.

r-0029.notes: The JCO covers most residential units not regulated by the RSO. It can apply to buildings newer than Oct 1, 1978 and to a single-family property. The RSO covers buildings first built on or before Oct 1, 1978 and has its own just-cause rules. The pre-1978 cutoff is therefore not a JCO test, and no test is written for it. Per the related RSO record, RSO covers pre-1978 buildings and JCO covers the rest, so the JCO fits when the certificate of occupancy is after Oct 1, 1978. That cutoff is not stated as a JCO exemption and is not encoded.

r-0030.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO

tests.source_text: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, ... some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance-abuse treatment centers
tests.note: JCO exemptions from the related record. RSO covers units built on or before Oct 1, 1978 and the JCO covers most other residential properties, so together nearly all residential rentals are covered apart from these exclusions.

tests.source_text: Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
tests.note: JCO applicability depends on tenancy length, which the data cannot see. RSO units have no such threshold.

r-0030.notes: Rule covers RSO units (built on or before Oct 1, 1978) and non-RSO units under the JCO, so no year cutoff test is applied. Qualified-tenant status, Mom & Pop reduced amounts, resident-manager and disaster exemptions concern amounts or tenant circumstances the data cannot see, so no tests were written for them.

r-0031.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) allowable rent increases

tests.source_text: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978
tests.note: Replacement units under LAMC 151.28 are also covered but cannot be detected from the data; year_built is a proxy for the certificate-of-occupancy date.

tests.source_text: rooms in hotels or rooming houses occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days
tests.note: Only hotel rooms occupied more than 30 consecutive days are covered, so transient occupancy is excluded.

tests.source_text: Rent amount is not regulated for condominium and townhome tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995.
tests.note: Condo and townhome units whose tenancy began after 1995 are not rent regulated. The engine cannot see the tenancy start date, so this is unknown for condos. The test is only meaningful when building_type is condo.

r-0031.notes: The coverage cutoff is the certificate-of-occupancy date of October 1, 1978. The luxury exemption (rent on or before May 31, 1978) and the market-rate cases after voluntary move-out, certain at-fault evictions or a buyout are unit-level facts the data cannot see, so no tests are written for them.

r-0032.title: LAMC Sec. 45.67 Prohibited Activities (source-of-income discrimination)
r-0032.notes: Coverage is any person offering, renting, or listing housing in the City of Los Angeles, with no exemptions and no building-level limits. The related records (RSO, JCO) define other ordinances' coverage, not this rule's, so they were not applied.

r-0033.title: Security deposit interest for RSO units (LAMC 151.06.02)

tests.source_text: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978
tests.note: Coverage text only says 'subject to LARSO'; the RSO cutoff comes from the related rent_increase_limits record. The certificate-of-occupancy date is not visible, so year_built is the proxy.

tests.source_text: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses
tests.note: Exclusion of non-residential and transient categories, taken from related RSO/JCO records.

r-0033.notes: Rule covers properties subject to LARSO. The RSO criteria are taken from the related rent_increase_limits record (first built on or before October 1, 1978). Condo and townhome rent exemptions for tenancies after 12/31/1995 concern rent amount and are not applied here. The luxury exemption cannot be evaluated from the data.

r-0034.title: H.5222 - An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
r-0034.notes: H.5222 is a pending bill and the status page does not reproduce its text, so its scope, coverage and exemptions are not in the capture. The related S.2983 record also states no coverage criteria. The engine should answer unknown. Check the bill text itself.

r-0035.title: S.2983 An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting (bill)
r-0035.notes: S.2983 is a bill history page only. The operative text, definitions and exemptions are not in this capture, so building-level coverage cannot be determined. The related H.5222 record lists no coverage conditions. The bill is also not enacted.

r-0036.title: Broker fee payable only by the party who engaged the broker
r-0036.notes: Coverage is defined by who is acting (licensed brokers/salespersons finding rental residential property), not by building characteristics. The rule has no stated exemptions and no building-level limits, so no tests are needed.

r-0037.title: No application fees by landlords (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B)
r-0037.notes: The rule covers lessors before a tenancy begins and states no building-level limits (year built, unit count, building type). The broker exemption turns on the licensing status of the person charging the fee, not on the building, so it cannot be tested from address data. The related security-deposit record exempts vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less. That is a tenancy-length fact the engine cannot see, and it comes from a different rule's text, so no test is written for it.

r-0040.title: Source-of-income / housing subsidy discrimination ban (M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10))
r-0040.notes: The ban applies to any person furnishing rental accommodations, and no building-level limits or exemptions are stated. The 100-day vacation-rental exclusion in the related security deposit record belongs to c. 186 § 15B and not to this rule, so no test was written for it.

r-0041.title: Massachusetts security deposit limits and handling (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B)

tests.value: tenancy longer than 100 days or not for vacation/recreational purpose
tests.source_text: does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy or tenancy of one hundred days or less in duration which is for a vacation or recreational purpose
tests.note: Short-term (100 days or less) vacation or recreational rentals are exempt. The engine cannot see rental duration or purpose, so this is not checkable from address data.

r-0041.notes: Statewide statute covering residential leases and tenancies-at-will, with no building-type, unit-count, age, or owner limits. The only exemption is short-term vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less, which is a use fact not visible in address data.

r-0042.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act

tests.source_text: Residential dwelling unit excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.
tests.note: Excludes inpatient medical, licensed long-term care, and detention/correctional facilities; an ordinary apartment building passes.

r-0042.notes: The act covers owners of one or more rental residential dwelling units, so there is no unit-count or age limit. The software and algorithm exemptions (human-analysis spreadsheets, public rent estimators, listing databases, government affordability programs) concern the tool used, not the building, and cannot be tested from address facts. Not yet effective: the effective date is 2027-07-01, after the 2026-10-01 query date.

r-0043.title: Residential rental application fee cap (P.L. 2025, c.405)

tests.source_text: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent
tests.note: Exemption for one-family and two-family dwellings. Single_family and duplex are used as proxies for these. Units in larger buildings are covered.

tests.source_text: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent
tests.note: A building with one or two units is exempt. Only buildings with 3 or more units are covered.

tests.source_text: New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensees, unless the licensee is the landlord of the property
tests.note: Concerns the identity and licensing of the person charging the fee. It cannot be seen at the address level.

r-0043.notes: Rule in force since 2026-05-01. The $50 cap applies to residential rentals other than one- or two-family dwellings. The licensee exemption depends on who charges the fee and cannot be determined from address data.

r-0044.title: Anti-Eviction Act (good cause required)

tests.source_text: does not apply to hotel or motel guests or guest houses rented to transient or seasonal tenants
tests.note: Hotel/motel/transient/seasonal exclusion; apartment buildings pass.

tests.source_text: May not apply to owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units
tests.note: Owner occupancy is not visible in the data, so the engine cannot confirm. The exception is impossible when the building has more than 2 units.

tests.source_text: does not apply to a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it
tests.note: Trust or family-occupancy status cannot be seen from address data.

r-0044.notes: Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings fall under N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2 with a narrower list of grounds; the rule still applies there in a limited form. The 2-unit owner-occupied exemption is the hard exclusion. Coverage is otherwise broad (single-family, mobile homes, apartments, rooming/boarding houses).

r-0045.title: Anti-Eviction Act: good cause required for lease non-renewal

tests.source_text: motels or hotels, and transient or seasonal units
tests.note: Hotels, motels and transient or seasonal units are excluded; an apartment building passes this test.

tests.source_text: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (which have a separate section)
tests.note: Owner occupancy is not visible in the data, so the engine cannot check it. The exemption applies only to two- or three-family dwellings, so buildings with more than 3 units cannot qualify.

r-0045.notes: Coverage is residential rentals generally. The list of good causes is in a later part of the guide and does not affect coverage. Related records describe the owner-occupied exemption as two or fewer rental units, but this rule's text says two- or three-family, so the rule's own wording is used.

r-0047.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income / rent payment protection

tests.source_text: Rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit
tests.note: Owner occupancy is not visible in the data. A two-family dwelling can be exempt only when the owner lives in the other unit. The exemption is impossible if the building has more than 2 units.

tests.source_text: rental of rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling
tests.note: Owner occupancy is not visible in the data. This room-rental exemption is only possible in a one-family dwelling, so it is impossible if the building has more than 1 unit.

r-0047.notes: Coverage is all property, residential and business, with exemptions. The religious-organization preference, housing for older persons, and one-sex residence carve-outs concern other protected classes (religion, familial status, sex) and do not limit the source-of-income provision, so they are not turned into tests.

r-0048.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act (criminal record screening limits)

tests.source_text: other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
tests.note: Exclusion applies only when the premises is owner-occupied AND has four or fewer units. The engine cannot see owner occupancy, so this is unknown unless the building has more than four units.

r-0048.notes: The only building-level limit is the exclusion of owner-occupied premises with not more than four dwelling units. Owner occupancy is not visible in the data, so it is expressed as an owner_type test that is defeated when units > 4. The federally assisted housing and sex offender registry provisions are permitted considerations, not coverage exemptions, so they get no tests.

r-0049.title: NJ Security Deposit Law: cap of 1.5 months' rent

tests.source_text: Owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units are excluded unless the tenant gives the landlord 30 days written notice invoking the act.
tests.note: Engine cannot see owner occupancy or whether the tenant gave written notice, so this is unknown. The exclusion applies only to owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units, and the guide also lists owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (tenant may opt in).

tests.source_text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
tests.note: Not applied: single-family rentals are covered. This test is invalid and should be disregarded.

r-0049.notes: Covers all rental premises used for dwelling purposes (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26). The only building-level limit is the owner-occupied exemption (two or fewer rental units absent tenant notice; two- or three-family owner-occupied per the guide), which turns on owner identity and tenant notice the data cannot see, so it is defeated if units exceed 3. The seasonal-rental carve-out (125 consecutive days or fewer) affects only the interest-account rules and is not a coverage test.

r-0050.title: Newark Rent Control: annual CPI-based rent increase cap

tests.source_text: hotel/motel space rented day-to-day to transients; commercial space
tests.note: Excludes transient hotel/motel and commercial space; apartments pass.

tests.source_text: newly constructed multiple dwellings ... The period is the amortization period of the initial mortgage or 30 years after completion of construction, whichever is less
tests.note: Exemption lasts the lesser of the mortgage amortization period or 30 years; 30 years is the maximum, so buildings under 30 years old may be exempt. The mortgage period is not visible, so this test is an upper-bound proxy.

tests.source_text: public housing; ... units under a contract with a governmental agency that regulates rent
tests.note: Subsidy and public housing status are not visible in the data, so the engine cannot check this.

r-0050.notes: Coverage is limited to multiple dwellings (§ 19:2-2.1). The definition of multiple dwelling in § 19:2-2 is not quoted, so no unit-count threshold is set. The newly constructed exemption is the lesser of the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years, so the 30-year test is an approximation. Vacant dwellings, rehabilitated Section 8 units and the 25% ceiling are not building-level tests.

r-0051.title: Newark Ban the Box - Housing (criminal record check practices)

tests.source_text: excludes (1) a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit
tests.note: Owner occupancy of the other unit in a two-family dwelling is not visible in the data. A duplex is the only building type where this exclusion could apply.

tests.source_text: a room or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling
tests.note: Owner occupancy of a one-family dwelling is not visible in the data. This exclusion could only apply to single-family buildings.

tests.source_text: property designated for a government program that encourages housing for people with criminal histories
tests.note: Program designation is not visible in the data.

r-0051.notes: The two owner-occupancy exclusions are encoded separately, each defeated when the building type rules it out. The exemption for cases where federal or state law requires or permits consideration of criminal history is not an address-level fact, so no test is written for it. The related rent control record gives no coverage criteria for this rule.

r-0052.title: San Diego Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price Fixing (SDMC §98.1103)

tests.source_text: software used to set rents or income limits under local, state or federal affordable housing program guidelines
tests.note: The exemption covers software used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing programs. The engine cannot see subsidy status, so the answer is unknown for these properties.

r-0052.notes: The rule covers all residential rental property in San Diego, with no limits on building type, age or unit count. The software exemptions (aggregated historical reports, appraisal software) concern the type of product, not the building, so they are not tests. The affordable-housing program exemption applies to software use and is recorded as a funding test the data cannot see.

r-0053.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause for termination of tenancy)

tests.source_text: Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt (unless a mobilehome).
tests.note: Year_built is a proxy; the exact certificate-of-occupancy date is unknown.

tests.source_text: Transient/tourist hotels; mobilehomes subject to the MRL; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care or licensed elder care and nonprofit transitional housing; school-owned dormitories
tests.note: Excluded categories; an apartment building passes.

tests.source_text: owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex
tests.note: Owner occupancy is not visible in the data. This exemption is impossible for buildings with more than 2 units.

tests.source_text: separately alienable units (e.g., condo) not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, with written exemption notice
tests.note: Condos and single-family homes are exempt only when the owner is not a corporate-type entity and written notice was given. Owner identity and notice are not visible in the data.

tests.source_text: deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (but not Section 8)
tests.note: Subsidy and deed-restriction status are not visible in the data.

tests.source_text: Residential rental property with a tenancy of more than 30 days
tests.note: Tenancy length is not visible in the data.

r-0053.notes: The certificate-of-occupancy test uses year_built as a proxy. The shared bath/kitchen with owner exemption is not representable. Section 8 tenants are not exempt.

r-0054.title: San Diego Prohibition of Discrimination Based on a Tenant's Source of Income

tests.source_text: Does not apply where the owner or a family member resides in the same residential building and shares a bathroom or kitchen facility with the tenant or prospective tenant (§98.0804).
tests.note: Owner/family shared-facility exemption cannot be determined from assessor data; engine should treat as unknown.

r-0054.notes: Coverage is defined by reference to Municipal Code section 98.0720, whose text is not in the corpus. Related just-cause and algorithmic-pricing records describe different rules, so their coverage limits were not borrowed. The only stated exemption is the owner/family shared-facility case, which is not visible in the data. The program-compliance exception is an act-level carve-out and not a building-level test.

r-0055.title: S.F. Rent Ordinance Section 37.10C - Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent-Setting Devices
r-0055.notes: The ban covers residential units in San Francisco generally. No building-level limits or exemptions are stated. The definition of 'algorithmic device' describes the software, not the building, so it is not a test on any address fact. The just-cause and rent-limit cutoffs (certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979) apply to those rules, not to this one.

r-0056.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction (S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a))
r-0056.notes: Coverage is defined only as units covered by the Rent Ordinance, which would be circular as a test. Neither this rule nor the related records state the Ordinance's actual building-level criteria (the rent-increase-limits record says coverage thresholds are not stated). The coverage text lists the June 13, 1979 certificate of occupancy cutoff and Costa-Hawkins only as units exempt from rent increase limits that remain subject to just cause, so these are inclusions and get no exclusion tests. The D082 exemption (temporary capital improvement evictions under 20 days governed by Civ. Code 1947.9) concerns the type of eviction, not building characteristics, so no test is created.
r-0056.explanation_note: statutory exemptions (certain owner-occupied shared units, institutional housing) not testable from county data
r-0056.review_ruling: instructions/rulings_05.md #1: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9 just-cause protection extends to units regardless of construction date; D079 states inclusions, not exclusions. Treat coverage as all residential rental units in SF. Remaining statutory exemptions are not testable from parcel data and rare in a 5+ unit sample.

r-0057.title: San Francisco annual allowable rent increase (3/1/2026\u20132/28/2027)

tests.source_text: newly constructed units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979
tests.note: Related just-cause record says units with a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt from rent increase limits, so the rule covers buildings with a CO on or before that date. The engine uses year_built as a proxy, with the cutoff year treated as unknown.

tests.source_text: tenancies eligible for a rent increase under Costa-Hawkins
tests.note: Costa-Hawkins exemption (single-family homes and condos). The related record names it only loosely, so this is a weak inference and is flagged here; if the engine disagrees, drop this test.

r-0057.notes: The rule's own coverage text is circular (rent-controlled units subject to the Rent Ordinance), so the tests come from the related just-cause record. Tenancies regulated by another government agency or eligible for Costa-Hawkins increases cannot be seen in address data.

r-0058.title: Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
r-0058.notes: The rule is limited to affordable housing decisions, but the page gives no thresholds or other operative details. The related records do not explain who is covered by or exempt from this ordinance. 'Affordable housing' status (subsidy or deed restriction) cannot be seen in address data, so the engine should answer unknown rather than applies.

r-0059.title: SF security deposit interest rate
r-0059.notes: The rule covers residential tenancies subject to SF security deposit interest rules. The document states no thresholds and no exemptions. Related records describe Rent Ordinance coverage, not this rule's category, so no building-level tests were derived from them.

r-0060.title: Santa Ana Ordinance NS-3090 (automated rent price-fixing)
r-0060.notes: Coverage is all apartment owners and landlords and residential rental property in Santa Ana, with no unit-count or building-level thresholds stated. The exemption in D087 (pricing software that uses only public data or aggregate historical data, or tools used for affordable housing compliance) concerns the software used, not the building, so no address-level test applies. The related just-cause and rent-stabilization exclusions are specific to those ordinances and are not used for this rule.

r-0061.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance

tests.source_text: Housing produced in the last 15 years
tests.note: New construction is exempt for 15 years, so the rule applies only when the building is at least 15 years old. year_built is used as a proxy.

tests.source_text: hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; and other shared living quarters
tests.note: Excludes non-residential and shared living categories.

tests.source_text: deed-restricted affordable housing
tests.note: Deed restriction status is not visible in the address data.

r-0061.notes: The 30-day tenancy threshold only sets when protection begins and is not a building-level test. The 1995 cutoff in the rent stabilization record applies to the rent cap and is not used here.

r-0062.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance

tests.source_text: the cap does not apply to residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995
tests.note: Full-date cutoff treated as a certificate-of-occupancy cutoff; buildings constructed after Feb 1, 1995 are exempt, so the rule covers buildings up to that date.

r-0062.notes: The mobile home space exemption (offered for rent after January 1, 1990) cannot be tested with the available building facts. The owner petition for fair return relief is an individual relief process and not a building-level exemption, so it is not turned into a test. The just-cause 15-year new-construction exemption belongs to a different rule and is not applied here.
